Incremental policy ruleset chunk from file 'nl_rules_input.md' (1-based global rule indices 11–16).

Rules in this chunk:
11. A petrified creature is transformed into a solid inanimate substance. Any nonmagical object the petrified creature is wearing is also transformed into that substance. Any nonmagical object the petrified creature is carrying is also transformed into that substance. The petrified creature's weight becomes ten times its normal weight. The petrified creature ceases aging. A petrified creature cannot take actions or reactions. A petrified creature cannot move. A petrified creature cannot speak. A petrified creature is unaware of its surroundings. Attack rolls made against a petrified creature have advantage. A petrified creature fails any Strength saving throw. A petrified creature fails any Dexterity saving throw. A petrified creature has resistance to all damage types. A petrified creature is immune to the poisoned condition. A petrified creature is immune to disease. Any poison already present in the petrified creature's system at the time of petrification is suspended rather than neutralized; it does not progress and does not end.
12. A poisoned creature has disadvantage on attack rolls. A poisoned creature has disadvantage on ability checks.
13. A prone creature's only form of movement is crawling, unless it takes the action to stand up. When a prone creature stands up, the prone condition ends. A prone creature has disadvantage on attack rolls. An attack roll against a prone creature has advantage if the attacker's distance to the prone creature is 5 feet or less. An attack roll against a prone creature has disadvantage if the attacker's distance to the prone creature is greater than 5 feet.
14. A restrained creature has a speed of 0. A restrained creature cannot gain any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls made against a restrained creature have advantage. Attack rolls made by a restrained creature have disadvantage. A restrained creature has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
15. A stunned creature cannot take actions or reactions. A stunned creature cannot move. A stunned creature can only speak falteringly; it cannot speak in a deliberate or coherent manner. A stunned creature fails any Strength saving throw. A stunned creature fails any Dexterity saving throw. Attack rolls made against a stunned creature have advantage.
16. An unconscious creature cannot take actions or reactions. An unconscious creature cannot move. An unconscious creature cannot speak. An unconscious creature is unaware of its surroundings. An unconscious creature releases any object it is holding at the moment it becomes unconscious. An unconscious creature falls prone at the moment it becomes unconscious. An unconscious creature fails any Strength saving throw. An unconscious creature fails any Dexterity saving throw. Attack rolls made against an unconscious creature have advantage. Any attack roll that hits an unconscious creature is a critical hit if the attacker's distance to the unconscious creature is 5 feet or less.
